claims.text: THE LORING TRAFFIC NEVER SAYS UFO. Its vocabulary is 'unidentified helicopter', 'intruder' and 'AFB Penetration' throughout. The NORAD logs do say UFO, repeatedly, in their own voice. The distinction belongs in the node, because the strength of the Loring material is that it is a nuclear security record rather than a UFO record.

claims.text: A NAMING DISCREPANCY INSIDE NORAD'S OWN RECORDS, UNRESOLVED. The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 10 November 1975 records the sighting at 'Minot Air Force Station' and says the object 'passed over the radar station'. The CINCNORAD four-part message of 11 November 1975 instead lists 'Minot AFB, ND'. Minot Air Force Station is a radar site and is not the 91st Strategic Missile Wing's missile field. Nothing opened by this board resolves which installation the sequence means, and this board does not choose one.

claims.text: The 1975 record at this installation is a continuous operational log, not a report. The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log covers 7 to 19 November 1975 with timed entries naming missile sites M-1, L-3, Lima, L-6, K-1, K-4, L-1, E-1, M-8, R-3 and R-4, the Harlowton launch control facility, radar track J330, and two F-106s scrambled at 0754Z on 8 November. Its final entry is marked in the original as the last pertaining to these incidents.

claims.sourceText: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 8 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The non-interception detail that the board's existing claim attributes to FOIA case 97-F-1677 is independently corroborated by the log's own words: '8 Nov 75 (0905Z) - From SAC CP: L-sites had fighters and objects; fighters did not get down to objects.' and '8 Nov 75 (0915Z) - From SAC CP: From four different points: Observed objects and fighters; when fighters arrived in the area, the lights went out; when fighters departed, the lights came back on; to NCOC.' Note that The Black Vault's landing page for 97-F-1677 reproduces no document text, so the log is the better citation for this claim.

claims.sourceText: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE LOG RECORDS ITS OWN NEGATIVES, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH TIER 1. After the 7 Nov 1327Z entry it notes: 'all this time, surveillance has not been able to detect any sort of track except for known traffic.' On 9 Nov 0320Z the FAA watch supervisor reported five air carriers in the vicinity and United Flight 157 reported seeing a meteor, arc welder's blue in colour. On 12 Nov 0251Z: 'Reported that both objects have disappeared. Never had any joy (contact) on radar.'

claims.sourceText: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 19 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The log's final entry is marked in the original as the last pertaining to these incidents: '19 Nov 75 (1327Z) - SAC command post report UFO observed by FSC & a cook, observed object travelling NE between M-8 and M-l at a fast rate of speed. Object bright white light seen 45 to 50 sec following terrain 200 ft off ground. The light was two to three times brighter than landing lights on a jet.'

claims.sourceText: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The log opens: '7 Nov 75 (1035Z) - Received a call from the 341st Strategic Air Command Post (SAC CP), saying that the following missile locations reported seeing a large red to orange to yellow objects M-l, L-3, LIMA and L-6. The general object location would be 10 miles south of Moore, Montana, and 20 miles east of Buffalo, Montana. Commander and Deputy for Operations (DO) informed.'

claims.sourceText: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 8 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The interception sequence is in the log's own words. '8 Nov 75 (0753Z) - J330 unknown 0753. Stationary/seven knots/12,000... two F-106, GTF, SCR 0754. NCOC notified.' '8 Nov 75 (0820Z) - Lost radar contact, fighters broken off at 0825.' '8 Nov 75 (0905Z) - From SAC CP: L-sites had fighters and objects; fighters did not get down to objects.' '8 Nov 75 (0915Z) - From SAC CP: From four different points: Observed objects and fighters; when fighters arrived in the area, the lights went out; when fighters departed, the lights came back on; to NCOC.'

claims.sourceText: CINCNORAD message as excerpted at http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm , against the 24th NORAD Region log, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , both opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: Minot recurs in the 1975 sequence, nine years after the 1966 incursions, but the two NORAD documents disagree about which Minot installation is meant. CINCNORAD's four-part message of 11 November 1975 lists 'Minot AFB, ND'; the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 10 November 1975 records the sighting at 'Minot Air Force Station' and says the object 'passed over the radar station'. The board carries the discrepancy rather than folding the radar-station entry into the missile-field record.

claims.sourceText: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 10 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt ; CINCNORAD message of 11 November 1975 as excerpted at http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm ; both opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE NAMING DISCREPANCY, STATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 10 November 1975 reads: 'UFO sighting reported by Minot Air Force Station, a bright star-like object in the West, moving east, about the size of a car. First seen approximately 1015Z. Approximately 1120Z the object passed over the radar station, 1,000 feet to 2,000 feet high, no noise heard. Three people from the site or local area saw the object.' The CINCNORAD four-part message of 11 November 1975 instead lists 'Minot AFB, ND'. Minot Air Force Station is a radar site and is not the 91st Strategic Missile Wing's missile field. No opened record resolves which installation the 1975 sequence means.

The contemporaneous-paper half of that split is real and checkable. It includes the National Military Command Center's Memorandum for Record of 29 October 1975 on the Loring penetration; the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 7 to 19 November 1975; the Project Blue Book Minot file of October and November 1968 with seven AF Form 117 witness questionnaires; the Project Blue Book telephone log of 1 August 1965 for F. E. Warren; and the 379th Bombardment Wing historian's file of January 1979. All were opened by this board on 19 September 2026.

E. Warren 1965 Blue Book log, https://rr0.org/time/2/0/0/6/02/24/Hastings_UfosightingsAtIcbmSites/Warren_1965/ ; all opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE COUNTERWEIGHT, ON THE SAME NODE. His method is not testimony alone, and the documentary half of his output is checkable and largely checks out. This board independently opened and read in full the 341st Strategic Missile Wing histories he relies on, the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for November 1975 that he republishes, and the F. E. Warren AFB Project Blue Book telephone log of 1 August 1965 first published by J. Allen Hynek in 1972. All three are real, and say what he says they say. The board grades the document half and the interview half of his output differently inside the same node.
